sizing_fixed_loss:
Fixed-loss sizing translates a standard linear payout of "I will risk x to make y" into an options package with a comparable sizing budget. The "Risk 1 to make" slider adjusts the amount at risk per unit of target profit.

Given this input and a target, we use the implied loss in your bet to set a sizing budget for the options structures we price, using premium or, where appropriate, a stress-loss estimate. This budget is not a guaranteed maximum loss. Some structures have unlimited losses, so you can lose more than the premium paid; please bear this in mind.

To make the numbers more intuitive, we size all structures relative to an amount of capital, W, which is a shared capital input across chats.
sizing_kelly:
We also size trades using the Kelly criterion. This method determines an optimal trade size based on your edge; you can learn more about it [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_criterion). To use it, we need your view across the full distribution of potential outcomes so that we can quantify how it differs from the market-implied distribution. If this is unclear, drop us a line—we are happy to help.

To make the numbers more intuitive, we size all structures relative to capital W, the total portfolio capital you deploy; this is a shared capital input across chats. Our implementation aims to maximise long-term compounded capital growth, based on your estimated probabilities; W is not the loss tolerance for a single trade.
what:
MacroTool is a decision-support platform for translating a directional market view into specific derivative structures. It gives traders a repeatable framework for comparing different ways to express the same view, improving consistency and speed without replacing a trader’s judgement.

**The platform provides:**
- Structure comparison across 50+ candidate strategies
- Scenario- and preference-based P&L analysis to show how trades behave under different outcomes
- Kelly-based position sizing and risk-budget-based sizing
- An AI assistant for natural-language questions about trade selection, risk/reward and analytics

The tool works on mobile but is designed for desktop.
how:
MacroTool uses a scoring framework designed to reflect how experienced traders translate a view into a trade, rather than relying solely on measures such as expected P&L, breakeven levels or back-testing.

**Recommendations are deterministic, not AI-generated.** With the same view, market data, preferences and engine configuration, the tool produces the same results every time. We build, test and tune the framework, which supplies every calculated number and recommendation. The LLM provides only the conversational interface; it is not the pricing or risk engine.

**Current limitations:** pricing is intended for directional comparison and ranking rather than execution-grade quotes, and we continue to refine it. Market data is as of the date indicated, not live. Results support decision-making; they do not replace independent judgement or trade validation.
who: We are a team of traders with more than 40 years of combined buy-side and sell-side experience in market-making, structuring and risk management across FX options—from vanilla to hybrid products, and from developed to emerging markets. We started building MacroTool to simplify how we use this product set to construct trades that express market views.
